match.detail: no rule of the class wins a declaration on an element of any captured cell

entries.reason: Each class that styles nothing in any cell, or whose rules matched and lost, found by the browser instead of listed by hand.

CSS clips nothing here (`overflow` is `visible` initially, CSS Overflow 3 §3) and the set's root casts no shadow in any cell, so the capture-backed root leaves its layers unclipped, and a ring at its edge shows as in the browser. A root that casts a shadow still clips, since Figma draws a spread only from a clipping frame (PR2).
